en.greeting: Hi! You already know went, saw and ate for yesterday. Today: a new form for your experiences and fresh news, with ever, never, just, already and yet. Let's go step by step.

steps.title: have/has + the third form
steps.text: Indonesian says pernah, sudah and belum. English uses a new form for this: have/has + the third form of the verb.
steps.body: This is the **present perfect**: **have/has + third form**. Use it for something that happened **before now** when you **don't say when**: experiences (*pernah*) and fresh news (*sudah, baru saja, belum*). **have** with I, you, we, they; **has** with he, she, it. Every verb has three forms: base, past and **third form** (bentuk ketiga, the **past participle**). Regular verbs: the third form = the past (*worked*). These irregular verbs have a **new** third form, with no rule: learn them. Never use the past here: *I have seen*, not 'I have saw'.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Sari's email to her manager is ready to send.

question.prompt: Complete: Sari ___ an email to her manager.
question.explanation: Sari = she → **has**, then the **third form**: write → wrote → **written**. 'has wrote' uses the past form (the most common mistake), and 'have' is for I, you, we, they.

steps.title: Have you ever…?
steps.text: Now let's talk about experiences: things you have done (or not) in your life.
steps.body: **Have you ever + third form?** = Apakah kamu pernah…? Short answers: **Yes, I have.** / **No, I haven't.** (haven't = have not). **never** = belum/tidak pernah: *I have never eaten durian.* never already means 'not', so not 'I haven't never'. **Trap:** *Saya pernah ke Bali* = **I have been to Bali**, with no ever: ever is for questions. For places, say **been to** (went there and came back). Why not went? After have/has you always need the third form, and went is the past.

steps.title: Talking about experiences
steps.text: Here are some people talking about their lives. Notice what happens when they say when.
steps.body: The experience uses **have/has + third form**. When you add **when** it happened (a finished time like *last year*), switch to the **past simple**: *I went there last year*, not 'I have been there last year'. Note: *Budi has **gone** to Bali* = he is in Bali now; *has **been*** = he went and came back.

examples.en: Have you ever been to Lombok? — Yes, I have.
I went there last year with my family.
examples.id: Saya ke sana tahun lalu bersama keluarga.

examples.en: Bu Ani has never done yoga.
I've been to Malaysia twice.
examples.id: Saya sudah dua kali ke Malaysia.

examples.en: Have you ever written a letter in English? — No, never.
examples.id: Kamu pernah menulis surat dalam bahasa Inggris? — Belum pernah.

steps.title: Said when? Past simple
steps.text: Two ways to talk about the past. The question is: do you say when?

timeline.title: Past simple or present perfect?
timeline.caption: A finished time (yesterday, last week, two days ago) → past simple: I saw it two days ago. No time, and it matters now → have/has + third form: I have seen it.

marks.label: two days ago: I saw the film
some time before now: I have seen the film

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: You want to ask a new colleague: 'Kamu pernah ke Yogyakarta?'

options: Have you ever went to Yogyakarta?
Have you ever been to Yogyakarta?
Did you ever been to Yogyakarta?
question.explanation: pernah ke = **have been to**. After have you need the third form **been**, not the past **went**. 'Did you ever been' mixes did with the third form: did goes with the base verb.

steps.title: Build the sentence
steps.text: Rina is talking about her mother. In Jakarta it's always hot.

question.prompt: Arrange the words: Ibuku belum pernah melihat salju.
question.solution: My mother has never seen snow.
question.explanation: belum pernah = **never**, between **has** and the third form: **has never seen** (see → saw → seen). My mother = she → has.

steps.title: just, already, yet
steps.text: Three small words for fresh news. You already use them in Indonesian every day.
steps.body: **just** = baru saja, **already** = sudah, **not … yet** = belum. In questions, **yet** = sudah … belum? **just** and **already** go **between have/has and the third form**: *She has just arrived. I've already paid.* **yet** goes **at the end**, only in negatives and questions: *I haven't finished yet. Have you eaten yet?* Answers: **Yes, I have.** / **No, not yet.** Trap: *Saya sudah selesai* has no helper word, but English needs one: **I've already finished**, not 'I already finish'. Short forms: **I've** = I have, **she's** = she has (before a third form), **hasn't** = has not.

steps.title: Listen and answer
steps.text: Your boss asks you something about a client. Press play and listen.

question.listen: Have you called Pak Hasan yet?
question.prompt: Listen to your boss's question. You want to say 'Ya, baru saja saya telepon.' Choose your answer.
question.explanation: Your boss asks **Have you called Pak Hasan yet?** baru saja = **just**, between have and the third form: **I've just called him.** 'I just call him' has no have and no third form, and 'yesterday' is a finished time, so it can't go with have called.

steps.title: Quick review
steps.text: Flip through these cards to lock in the third forms and the new words.

flashcards.back: worked · visited · bought (same as the past)
Have you ever been to Bali?

flashcards.front: Saya belum pernah naik kereta api.
flashcards.back: I have never taken a train.
Have you eaten yet? — No, not yet.
I saw it yesterday. (finished time → past simple)

steps.title: Cheat sheet
steps.text: Here's everything on one page. Keep it for later.

artifact.title: Cheat sheet · present perfect
artifact.intro: have/has + third form, for experiences (ever, never) and fresh news (just, already, yet). Regular verbs: the third form = the past.
tips: **have** with I, you, we, they; **has** with he, she, it. Always the third form after it: **I have seen**, not 'I have saw'.
**ever** in questions (pernah), **never** = belum pernah. **just / already** go between have and the third form; **yet** goes at the end of negatives and questions.
A finished time (yesterday, last week, … ago) → past simple: **I saw it yesterday**, not 'I have seen it yesterday'.

I have never eaten durian.
She has just arrived.
We haven't paid yet.
I've seen this film. I saw it last week.

steps.title: Learn more
steps.text: Want more? Two short BBC videos (one on ever/never, one on just/already/yet) and a British Council page with practice tests. They are a little above this lesson's level, so turn on the subtitles.

id.greeting: Hai! Kamu sudah tahu went, saw dan ate untuk cerita kemarin. Hari ini: bentuk baru untuk pengalaman dan kabar terbaru, dengan ever, never, just, already dan yet. Ayo kita pelajari pelan-pelan.

steps.title: have/has + bentuk ketiga
steps.text: Bahasa Indonesia memakai pernah, sudah dan belum. Bahasa Inggris memakai bentuk baru untuk ini: have/has + bentuk ketiga kata kerja.
steps.body: Ini namanya **present perfect**: **have/has + bentuk ketiga**. Pakai untuk hal yang terjadi **sebelum sekarang** saat kamu **tidak menyebut kapan**: pengalaman (*pernah*) dan kabar baru (*sudah, baru saja, belum*). **have** untuk I, you, we, they; **has** untuk he, she, it. Setiap kata kerja punya tiga bentuk: dasar, lampau dan **bentuk ketiga** (**past participle**). Kata kerja beraturan: bentuk ketiga = bentuk lampau (*worked*). Kata kerja tidak beraturan ini punya bentuk ketiga yang **baru**, tanpa aturan: hafalkan. Jangan pakai bentuk lampau di sini: *I have seen*, bukan 'I have saw'.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Email Sari untuk manajernya sudah siap dikirim.

question.prompt: Lengkapi: Sari ___ an email to her manager.
question.explanation: Sari = she → **has**, lalu **bentuk ketiga**: write → wrote → **written**. 'has wrote' memakai bentuk lampau (kesalahan yang paling sering), dan 'have' untuk I, you, we, they.

steps.title: Have you ever…?
steps.text: Sekarang kita bicara tentang pengalaman: hal yang pernah (atau belum pernah) kamu lakukan dalam hidupmu.
steps.body: **Have you ever + bentuk ketiga?** = Apakah kamu pernah…? Jawaban singkat: **Yes, I have.** / **No, I haven't.** (haven't = have not). **never** = belum/tidak pernah: *I have never eaten durian.* never sudah berarti 'tidak', jadi bukan 'I haven't never'. **Jebakan:** *Saya pernah ke Bali* = **I have been to Bali**, tanpa ever: ever untuk pertanyaan. Untuk tempat, pakai **been to** (pernah ke sana dan sudah kembali). Kenapa bukan went? Setelah have/has selalu perlu bentuk ketiga, dan went itu bentuk lampau.

steps.title: Bercerita tentang pengalaman
steps.text: Ini beberapa orang bercerita tentang hidup mereka. Perhatikan apa yang terjadi saat mereka menyebut kapan.
steps.body: Pengalamannya memakai **have/has + bentuk ketiga**. Kalau kamu menambah **kapan** terjadinya (waktu yang sudah selesai seperti *last year*), ganti ke **past simple**: *I went there last year*, bukan 'I have been there last year'. Catatan: *Budi has **gone** to Bali* = dia sekarang ada di Bali; *has **been*** = dia pernah ke sana dan sudah kembali.

I went there last year with my family.

steps.title: Ada kapan-nya? Past simple
steps.text: Dua cara membicarakan masa lalu. Pertanyaannya: apakah kamu menyebut kapan?

timeline.title: Past simple atau present perfect?
timeline.caption: Waktu yang sudah selesai (yesterday, last week, two days ago) → past simple: I saw it two days ago. Tanpa waktu, dan penting sekarang → have/has + bentuk ketiga: I have seen it.

marks.label: two days ago: I saw the film
kapan saja sebelum sekarang: I have seen the film

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Kamu ingin bertanya ke rekan kerja baru: 'Kamu pernah ke Yogyakarta?'

options: Have you ever went to Yogyakarta?
Have you ever been to Yogyakarta?
Did you ever been to Yogyakarta?
question.explanation: pernah ke = **have been to**. Setelah have perlu bentuk ketiga **been**, bukan bentuk lampau **went**. 'Did you ever been' mencampur did dengan bentuk ketiga: did dipakai dengan kata kerja dasar.

steps.title: Susun kalimatnya
steps.text: Rina bercerita tentang ibunya. Di Jakarta selalu panas.

question.prompt: Susun kata-katanya: Ibuku belum pernah melihat salju.
question.solution: My mother has never seen snow.
question.explanation: belum pernah = **never**, di antara **has** dan bentuk ketiga: **has never seen** (see → saw → seen). My mother = she → has.

steps.title: just, already, yet
steps.text: Tiga kata kecil untuk kabar baru. Dalam bahasa Indonesia kamu memakainya setiap hari.
steps.body: **just** = baru saja, **already** = sudah, **not … yet** = belum. Di pertanyaan, **yet** = sudah … belum? **just** dan **already** diletakkan **di antara have/has dan bentuk ketiga**: *She has just arrived. I've already paid.* **yet** diletakkan **di akhir**, hanya di kalimat negatif dan pertanyaan: *I haven't finished yet. Have you eaten yet?* Jawabannya: **Yes, I have.** / **No, not yet.** Jebakan: *Saya sudah selesai* tidak memakai kata bantu, tapi bahasa Inggris perlu: **I've already finished**, bukan 'I already finish'. Bentuk singkat: **I've** = I have, **she's** = she has (sebelum bentuk ketiga), **hasn't** = has not.

steps.title: Dengar dan jawab
steps.text: Bosmu menanyakan sesuatu tentang klien. Tekan play dan dengarkan.

question.listen: Have you called Pak Hasan yet?
question.prompt: Dengarkan pertanyaan bosmu. Kamu ingin bilang 'Ya, baru saja saya telepon.' Pilih jawabanmu.
question.explanation: Bosmu bertanya **Have you called Pak Hasan yet?** baru saja = **just**, di antara have dan bentuk ketiga: **I've just called him.** 'I just call him' tidak memakai have dan bentuk ketiga, dan 'yesterday' adalah waktu yang sudah selesai, jadi tidak bisa dipakai dengan have called.

steps.title: Ulangan singkat
steps.text: Balik kartu-kartu ini supaya bentuk ketiga dan kata-kata barunya makin melekat.
